summary.text: Frank Pallone Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 6th Congressional District, first elected to the U.S. House in 1988. A Long Branch native and attorney, he previously served on the Long Branch City Council and in the New Jersey Senate. He is the top Democrat on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, which he chaired in the 117th Congress, and his official biography highlights health care, environmental and consumer-protection work.

paragraphs.text: Pallone was born in Long Branch, New Jersey, where, according to his official biography, he began his political career and still lives.
He earned a B.A. from Middlebury College in 1973, an M.A. from Tufts University in 1974 and a J.D. from Rutgers University in 1978; Ballotpedia lists his profession as attorney.
He was elected to the Long Branch City Council in 1982 and to the New Jersey Senate, representing the Monmouth County coastline, in 1983, and was re-elected to the state Senate in 1987.
Pallone was elected to the U.S. House on November 8, 1988, from New Jersey's former 3rd District.
After the 1992 redistricting he was elected in the 6th District, which his office describes as covering most of Middlesex County and the Bayshore and oceanfront areas of Monmouth County.
As chairman of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health in 2010, he played a key role, according to his official biography, in authoring the Affordable Care Act.

He chaired the full Energy and Commerce Committee during the 117th Congress (2021-2022) and is now its top Democrat; the committee's jurisdiction includes health care, energy, environment, commerce, food and drug safety, consumer protection, and communications and technology.

His office credits him with legislation giving the Food and Drug Administration additional oversight tools over cosmetics, included in the fiscal year 2023 federal spending bill, and with efforts to ban offshore drilling and ocean dumping off New Jersey's coast.
Pallone married his wife Sarah in 1992, and they have three adult children, according to his official biography.
